headline: Spending on data center equipment worldwide rose 92% in the second quarter, as AI demand and higher memory prices pushed costs up.
score_reason: Industry research firm data read in full; the figure comes from the headline, the text gives no total. No reduction.
importance_line: Cloud companies, AI developers and server makers are spending much more, partly because memory costs more; the 92% is the research firm's estimate.
summary: Lightwave Online reports, citing research firm Dell'Oro Group, that data center capital spending rose 92% in the second quarter, as AI infrastructure investment grew across computing, storage, networking and physical facilities. Dell'Oro says higher memory and storage prices raised average server prices, and that AI model builders and "neocloud" providers (companies renting out AI computing power) were the fastest-growing customer groups.
notes: Data period is Q2 2026; the report itself is new.
